nodes.label: ergodic averages
nodes.title: Ergodic averages
nodes.visibility_reason: the Introduction is public by convention
nodes.statement_html:
Let \((X,\Sigma,\mu)\) be a \(\sigma\)-finite measure space. We say that \(T: X \to X\) is a measure preserving transformation if for every measurable \(A\subset X\) the set \(T^{-1}(A)\) is measurable and has the same measure as \(A\).

Let \(n\geq 1\) be an integer. Let \(\mathbf{f}=(f_l)_{l\in [n)}\) be an \(n\)-tuple of complex-valued measurable functions and let \((T_l)_{l\in [n)}\) be an \(n\)-tuple of measure preserving transformations on \(X\). For an integer \(N\geq 1\) and every \(x\in X\), define the multiple ergodic averages
\[M_{N}(\mathbf{f})(x) := \tfrac{1}{N}\sum_{i=0}^{N-1} \prod_{l=0}^{n-1} f_l(T_l^i x).\]

nodes.statement_html:
Let \(m,n\ge 1\) be integers, let \((X_i,\mu_i)\) and \((Y,\nu)\) be measure spaces, let \(p\in[1,\infty]\), and let \(T\) be an \(n\)-linear map on \(n\)-tuples of complex-valued simple functions with values in \(L^p(Y)\). For \(a\in[m)\) and \(i\in[n)\), let \(q_{a,i}\in[1,\infty]\), and assume
\[\|T(f_0,\ldots,f_{n-1})\|_{L^p(Y)}\le A_a\prod_{i\in[n)}\|f_i\|_{L^{q_{a,i}}(X_i)}.\]
Let \(\theta_a\ge 0\) satisfy \(\sum_{a\in[m)}\theta_a=1\), and define \(p_i\in[1,\infty]\) by
\[\tfrac1{p_i}=\sum_{a\in[m)}\tfrac{\theta_a}{q_{a,i}}.\]
Then \(T\) extends to an \(n\)-linear map from \(\prod_{i\in[n)}L^{p_i}(X_i)\) to \(L^p(Y)\) and
\[\|T(f_0,\ldots,f_{n-1})\|_{L^p(Y)}\le \prod_{a\in[m)}A_a^{\theta_a}\prod_{i\in[n)}\|f_i\|_{L^{p_i}(X_i)}.\]

\[(2^{-2},2^{-3},\ldots,2^{-n},2^{-n})\]

\[\sum_{i\in[n)}p_i^{-1}=\tfrac12\]
and, for every nonempty \(I\subset[n)\),
\[\sum_{i\in I}p_i^{-1}\ge 2^{|I|-n-1}.\]

\[\bigcap_{j\in [J)} {\rm ker}\Pi_j=\{0\}\, .\]
Then there is \(C>0\) such that the following holds. For \(j\in [J)\), let \(f_j\in W_0({\mathbb R}^{l_j})\). Then for each \(u\in {\mathbb R}^m\), the function
\[v\to \prod_{j\in [J)}f_j(\Pi_{j}(u,v))\]

\[f(u):=\int_{{\mathbb R}^l}\prod_{j\in [J)}f_j(\Pi_{j}(u,v))\, dv \, ,\]

\[\|f\|_{W_0}\le C\prod_{j\in[J)}\|f_j\|_{W_0}\, .\]

Let \(1\le k\le n-1\). Let \(\rho\in W_0({\mathbb R}^{k+1})\) be non-negative and \(\phi\in W_0({\mathbb R})\). Set for \(u\in{\mathbb R}^{k+2}\) and \(i\in [k+1)\)
\[K(u):=\int_{\mathbb R} \rho(u_{[k+1)\setminus i}, u_{k+1}-q) \phi(u_{i}+q) \phi(q) \, dq\, .\]
Then \(K\in W_0({\mathbb R}^{k+2})\) and for all \(\mathbf{F}\in\mathfrak{F}\)
\[\Theta_{k+1}(K)(\mathbf{F})\ge 0\, .\]

\[\Theta_{k+1}(K_\rho)(\mathbf{F}) \le \Theta_{k+1}(K_{\tilde{\rho}})(\mathbf{F})\]

nodes.label: M to K
nodes.title: M to K
nodes.statement_html:
Let \(k\in{\mathbb N}\) satisfy \(1\le k\le n\). Let \(M\in W_0(({\mathbb R}^2)^k)\). Define for \(z\in {\mathbb R}^{k+1}\),
\[K_k(M)(z)=\int_{{\mathbb R}^{k-1}} M((z_{l}+p_{l},p_{l})_{l\in [k-1)}, z_{k-1}+z_{k}-\Sigma(p),z_{k}-\Sigma(p))\,dp.\]
The integrand is in \(W_0({\mathbb R}^{k-1})\) for every \(z\in{\mathbb R}^{k+1}\). The argument of \(M\) is identified with an element of \(({\mathbb R}^2)^{k}\). Then \(K_k(M)\in W_0({\mathbb R}^{k+1})\) and
\[\|K_k(M)\|_1 \le \|M\|_1.\]

\[M(y)=\tilde{M}(y_{[k)\setminus i}) \phi^{\otimes 2}(y_{i}).\]
Then \(M\in W_0(({\mathbb R}^2)^k)\) and for all \(\mathbf{F}\in {\mathfrak{F}}\),
\[\Lambda_k(M)(\mathbf{F})\ge 0.\]

nodes.label: Cauchy-Schwarz at k

nodes.label: Cauchy-Schwarz at n-1
nodes.title: Cauchy-Schwarz at n-1
nodes.statement_html:
Let \(J\in{\mathbb N}\) with \(J\ge1\) and, for \(j\in [J)\), let \(\rho_j\in W_0(({\mathbb R}^2)^{n-1})\) and \(\varphi_j\in W_0({\mathbb R})\) be real valued. Let \(i \in [n-1)\). Define
\[M=\sum_{j\in [J)} \rho_j *_{e_i^0+e_i^1} (\varphi_j * \varphi_j),\]
and for \(y\in ({\mathbb R}^2)^n\),

Then \(M\in W_0(({\mathbb R}^2)^{n-1})\) and \(\tilde{M}\in W_0(({\mathbb R}^2)^n)\) and for all \(\mathbf{F}\in\mathfrak{F}\)
\[|\Lambda_{n-1}(M)(\mathbf{F})| \le \sup_{\mathbf{\tilde{F}}\in\mathfrak{F}}|\Lambda_{n}(\tilde{M})(\mathbf{\tilde{F}})|.\]

nodes.label: multiplicatively spaced monotone sequences
nodes.title: Multiplicatively spaced monotone sequences
nodes.statement_html:
A sequence \(a:{\mathbb Z}\to{\mathbb R}\) with \(a(j)>0\) for every \(j\in{\mathbb Z}\) is called multiplicatively spaced if, for each \(j\in{\mathbb Z}\)
\[2a(j)\le a(j+1)\, .\]
Let \({\rm A}\) be the set of such sequences.

nodes.label: Extension of sequences
nodes.title: Extension of sequences
nodes.statement_latex:

Then there is a unique $b\in A$ such that for all $j\in [J)$ we have $a(j)=b(j)$ and for $j\ge J$ we have $b(j)=2^{j-J+1} a(J-1)$ and for $j<0$ we have $b(j)=2^j a(0)$\, .

nodes.label: Operations on spaced sequences

(iv) If $c:{\mathbb Z}\to (0,\infty)$ is defined by $c(j)=\sqrt{a(j)^2+b(j)^2}$ for all $j\in{\mathbb Z}$, then $c\in {\rm A}$.

nodes.label: Distance of spaced sequences
nodes.title: Distance of spaced sequences
nodes.statement_html:
Given \(a,b\in {\rm A}\), define
\[\operatorname{dist}(a,b)=\min\{k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}\,:\,\forall j, a(j-k)\le b(j)\le a(j+k)\}\]
with the understanding that the value is \(\infty\) if there is no such \(k\).

nodes.label: Properties of distance of sequences
nodes.title: Properties of distance of sequences
nodes.statement_latex:
Let $a,b,c\in {\rm A}$.
Then

(i) If $\operatorname{dist}(a,b)=0$, then $a=b$.

(ii) $\operatorname{dist}(a,b)=\operatorname{dist}(b,a)$

(iii) $\operatorname{dist}(a,c)\le \operatorname{dist}(a,b)+\operatorname{dist}(b,c)$

(iv) If $c(j)=b(j+1)$, then $\operatorname{dist}(a,c)\le \operatorname{dist}(a,b)+1$.

(v) For all $t>0$, $\operatorname{dist}(t\cdot a,t\cdot b)=\operatorname{dist}(a,b)$

(vi) For all $h\in\mathbb{Z}$,
$\operatorname{dist}(a,2^h a)\le |h|$.

\[1-\mathfrak{g}(x)\le f(x)\le 1.\]

nodes.title: Lemma: L:derivative-estimate-for-G
nodes.statement_html:
Let \(N\in {\mathbb N}\), \(\nu\in [-1,0)\) and let \(H(x)=(1-x)^{\nu}-1\) for \(x\in [0,1)\). Then for \(x\in [0,e^{-3\pi/16}]\), we have
\[|H^{(N)}(x)| \leq C_{\href{nct-node:L%3Aderivative-estimate-for-G}{4.60},N},\]
where \(C_{\href{nct-node:L%3Aderivative-estimate-for-G}{4.60},N}= N! \left(1 - e^{-3\pi/16}\right)^{-(N+1)}\).

nodes.title: Lemma: L:faa-di-bruno

nodes.label: L:second-gaussian-estimate
nodes.title: Lemma: L:second-gaussian-estimate
used_by: constant mean four scale Gaussian kernel
nodes.statement_html:
Let \(c>0\), \(N\in \mathbb N\) and assume that \(\phi\) is a \(W_0({\mathbb R})\) function such that \(\widehat{\phi}\) is supported in \([-1,1]\) and equal to \(1\) on \([-1/2,1/2]\) and \(\widehat{\phi}\) is \(N\) times continuously differentiable and \(\max_{0\leq m \leq N} \|\widehat{\phi}^{(m)}\|_{\infty} \leq c\). Assume that \(0<\mu \leq \lambda \leq 1/2\), \(t\geq \sqrt{3}/2\) and \(\nu \in [-1,0)\). For \(\xi \in {\mathbb R}\), we define
\[R(\xi)=(\mathfrak{g}(\mu\xi))^{-1}\left(\widehat{\phi}(\lambda\xi)-\widehat{\phi}(\xi)\right)\left((1-\mathfrak{g}(t\xi))^{\nu} -1\right).\]
Then \(R\) is \(N\) times continuously differentiable and
\[(2\pi)^{-N} \max(\|R^{(N)}\|_1,\|R^{(N)}\|_\infty) \leq cC_{\href{nct-node:L%3Asecond-gaussian-estimate}{4.63},N},\]
where \(C_{\href{nct-node:L%3Asecond-gaussian-estimate}{4.63},N}=8\sum_{l=0}^N \binom{N}{l} (2\pi)^{l-N} C_{\href{nct-node:L%3Agaussian-bump-estimate}{4.58},l} C_{\href{nct-node:L%3Afaa-di-bruno}{4.61},N-l}\).

nodes.label: constant second gaussian estimate
nodes.title: constant C_L:second-gaussian-estimate,N

\[C_{\href{nct-node:L%3Asecond-gaussian-estimate}{4.63},N}\le2^{20(N+1)^3}.\]
Moreover,
\[C_{\href{nct-node:L%3Asecond-gaussian-estimate}{4.63},0}<\tfrac{313}{512}2^{14}<2^{14}, \qquad C_{\href{nct-node:L%3Asecond-gaussian-estimate}{4.63},1}<\tfrac{43}{64}2^{19}<2^{19},\]

nodes.label: L:gaussian-bump-decomposition
nodes.title: Lemma: L:gaussian-bump-decomposition
nodes.statement_html:
Let \(\phi\) be a \(W_0({\mathbb R})\) function such that \(\widehat{\phi}\) is supported in \([-1,1]\) and equal to \(1\) on \([-1/2,1/2]\). Let \(\mu_\pm,\lambda_\pm\in\mathbb R\) be positive and satisfy
\[2\mu_-\le 2\lambda_-\le \lambda_+\le \mu_+,\]
and let \( u\in [-1,0)\).

Define a function \( ho\) by
\[ ho = \mathcal F^{-1}\left(\xi \mapsto (\widehat{\phi}(\lambda_-\xi) - \widehat{\phi}(\lambda_+\xi)) (\mathfrak{g}(\mu_- \xi)-\mathfrak{g}(\mu_+\xi))^{ u} ight).\]
Also, for \(\xi \in {\mathbb R}\) we define
\[\varrho_0(\xi)=(\mathfrak{g}(\mu_{-}| u|^{1/2}\xi))^{-1}\widehat{\phi}(\lambda_{-}\xi)\]
\[\varrho_1(\xi)=-(\mathfrak{g}(\mu_{-}| u|^{1/2}\xi))^{-1}\widehat{\phi}(\lambda_{+}\xi)\]
\[\varrho_2(\xi)=(\mathfrak{g}(\mu_{-}| u|^{1/2}\xi))^{-1}\left(\widehat{\phi}(\lambda_{-}\xi)-\widehat{\phi}(\lambda_{+}\xi) ight)\left((1-\mathfrak{g}(t\xi))^{ u} -1 ight)\]
with \(t=\sqrt{\mu_{+}^2-\mu_{-}^2}\). Then \( ho\) is a well-defined continuous function and
\[ ho=\sum_{l\in [3)} \mathcal F^{-1} (\varrho_l).\]

nodes.label: four scale Gaussian kernel
nodes.title: four scale Gaussian kernel estimate
nodes.statement_latex:
Let $c>0$, $N\in \mathbb N$ with $N\geq 2$ and assume that $\phi$ is a $W_0({\mathbb R})$ function such that
$\widehat{\phi}$ is supported in $[-1,1]$ and equal to $1$ on $[-1/2,1/2]$ and $\widehat{\phi}$ is $N$ times continuously differentiable and $\max_{0\leq m \leq N} \|\widehat{\phi}^{(m)}\|_{\infty} \leq c$.
Let $\mu_\pm,\lambda_\pm\in\mathbb R$ be positive and satisfy~\eqref{E:assumption-on-mu-lambda}, let $\nu\in [-1,0)$ and let $\rho$ be defined by~\eqref{E:definition-rho}.
Then $\rho \in W_0({\mathbb R})$ and for every $x\in\mathbb{R}$,
\begin{equation} |\rho(x)| \le cC_{\ref{four scale Gaussian kernel},N} (\langle x\rangle^N_{(\lambda_-)} + \langle x\rangle^N_{(\lambda_+)}), \end{equation}
where
\begin{equation} C_{\ref{four scale Gaussian kernel},N} = 2C_{\ref{lem:smoothdecay2},N}\max(C_{\ref{L:gaussian-bump-estimate},0},C_{\ref{L:gaussian-bump-estimate},N}) +2^N\max(C_{\ref{L:second-gaussian-estimate},0},C_{\ref{L:second-gaussian-estimate},N}). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_html:
Let \(c>0\), \(N\in \mathbb N\) with \(N\geq 2\) and assume that \(\phi\) is a \(W_0({\mathbb R})\) function such that \(\widehat{\phi}\) is supported in \([-1,1]\) and equal to \(1\) on \([-1/2,1/2]\) and \(\widehat{\phi}\) is \(N\) times continuously differentiable and \(\max_{0\leq m \leq N} \|\widehat{\phi}^{(m)}\|_{\infty} \leq c\). Let \(\mu_\pm,\lambda_\pm\in\mathbb R\) be positive and satisfy (4.170), let \(\nu\in [-1,0)\) and let \(\rho\) be defined by (4.171). Then \(\rho \in W_0({\mathbb R})\) and for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}\),

where
\[C_{\href{nct-node:four%20scale%20Gaussian%20kernel}{4.66},N} = 2C_{\href{nct-node:lem%3Asmoothdecay2}{4.43},N}\max(C_{\href{nct-node:L%3Agaussian-bump-estimate}{4.58},0},C_{\href{nct-node:L%3Agaussian-bump-estimate}{4.58},N}) +2^N\max(C_{\href{nct-node:L%3Asecond-gaussian-estimate}{4.63},0},C_{\href{nct-node:L%3Asecond-gaussian-estimate}{4.63},N}).\]

nodes.label: constant four scale Gaussian kernel
nodes.title: constant C_four scale Gaussian kernel,N
nodes.statement_html:
For every \(N\in{\mathbb N}\),
\[C_{\href{nct-node:four%20scale%20Gaussian%20kernel}{4.66},N}\le2^{25(N+1)^3}.\]
Moreover,

nodes.label: mean four scale Gaussian kernel
nodes.title_tex: mean value four scale Gaussian kernel estimate
nodes.title: mean value four scale Gaussian kernel estimate
nodes.statement_latex:
Let $c>0$, $N\in \mathbb N$ with $N\geq 2$ and assume that $\phi$ is a $W_0({\mathbb R})$ function such that
$\widehat{\phi}$ is supported in $[-1,1]$ and equal to $1$ on $[-1/2,1/2]$ and $\widehat{\phi}$ is $N$ times continuously differentiable and $\max_{0\leq m \leq N} \|\widehat{\phi}^{(m)}\|_{\infty} \leq c$.
Let $\mu_\pm,\lambda_\pm\in\mathbb R$ be positive and satisfy~\eqref{E:assumption-on-mu-lambda}. Assume, in addition, that $\lambda_{+}=2\lambda_{-}$.
Let $\nu\in [-1,0)$ and let $\rho$ be defined by~\eqref{E:definition-rho}.
Then for all $x,y \in\mathbb{R}$,
\begin{equation}
|\rho(x+y)-\rho(x)| \le c C_{\ref{mean four scale Gaussian kernel},N} \min(1,2\pi \lambda_{+}^{-1}|y|) (\langle x+y\rangle^N_{(\lambda_+)}+
\langle x\rangle^N_{(\lambda_+)}),
\end{equation}
where
\begin{equation} C_{\ref{mean four scale Gaussian kernel},N} =  5\cdot 2^{N+1}\max_{0\leq l \leq N} C_{\ref{L:gaussian-bump-estimate},l} +2^{N+3}\max_{0\leq l \leq N} 2^lC_{\ref{L:second-gaussian-estimate},l}.\end{equation}

Then for all \(x,y \in\mathbb{R}\),

nodes.id: constant mean four scale Gaussian kernel
nodes.label: constant mean four scale Gaussian kernel

nodes.label: geometric parameters
nodes.title: geometric parameters
nodes.statement_latex:
Let $\Gamma$ be the set of triples $(k,u,a)$ with $k\in{\mathbb N}$, $1\le k\le n$, $u\in[2)^k$, $a\in ({\rm A}^{2})^k$  so that $\operatorname{dist}(a_{i}^0,a_{i}^1)<\infty$ for all $i\in [k)$.
For a sequence pair $\alpha=(\alpha_0,\alpha_1)\in {\rm A}^2$ we write $\Delta(\alpha) = \mathrm{dist}(\alpha_{0}, \alpha_1)$
and for $\gamma\in\Gamma$ let
\begin{equation} \Delta_\gamma= 1+\sum_{i\in [k)} \Delta(a_i). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_html:
Let \(\Gamma\) be the set of triples \((k,u,a)\) with \(k\in{\mathbb N}\), \(1\le k\le n\), \(u\in[2)^k\), \(a\in ({\rm A}^{2})^k\) so that \(\operatorname{dist}(a_{i}^0,a_{i}^1)<\infty\) for all \(i\in [k)\). For a sequence pair \(\alpha=(\alpha_0,\alpha_1)\in {\rm A}^2\) we write \(\Delta(\alpha) = \mathrm{dist}(\alpha_{0}, \alpha_1)\) and for \(\gamma\in\Gamma\) let
\[\Delta_\gamma= 1+\sum_{i\in [k)} \Delta(a_i).\]

nodes.label: auto:unitary-matrices-definition
nodes.title: two unitary matrices
nodes.statement_latex:
For $u\in [2)$ define unitary matrices $W_u\in{\mathbb R}^{2\times 2}$ as follows:
Let $W_0$ be the $2\times 2$ identity matrix and $W_1=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\begin{pmatrix}1 & 1\-1 & 1\end{pmatrix}$.
nodes.statement_html: For \(u\in [2)\) define unitary matrices \(W_u\in{\mathbb R}^{2\times 2}\) as follows: Let \(W_0\) be the \(2\times 2\) identity matrix and \(W_1=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\begin{pmatrix}1 & 1\-1 & 1\end{pmatrix}\).

nodes.label: double sequence of 2D functions
nodes.title: double sequence of 2D functions
nodes.statement_html:
For \(1\le k\le n\), let \(\mathcal{X}_k\) be the set of double sequences
\[X=(X_{i,j})_{i\in [k),j\in {\mathbb Z}}\]
with \(X_{i,j}\in W_0({\mathbb R}^2)\).

nodes.label: kernel sequences
nodes.title: kernel sequences
nodes.statement_html:
Let \(k\in{\mathbb N}\) with \(1\le k\le n\). Let \({\rm M}(k)\) be the space of sequences \(\mathbf{M}=(M_j)_{j\in {\mathbb Z}}\) such that for \(j\in {\mathbb Z}\) we have \(M_j\in W_0(({\mathbb R}^2)^k)\). Define
\[\|\mathbf{M}\|_{{\rm M}(k)}:=\sup_{J\in{\mathbb N},\,J\ge1,\,\mathbf{F}\in\mathfrak F}\min(1,J^{-1+2^{k-n+1}}) |\Lambda_k(\sum_{j\in [J)} M_j)(\mathbf{F})| \, .\]

nodes.label: 2D Gaussians
nodes.title: 2D Gaussians
nodes.statement_html:
For \(q\in{\mathbb R}^2\) with \(q_0,q_1>0\), \(u\in[2)\), and \(v\in\mathbb R^2\), define
\[G_{q,u}(v) = \mathfrak{g}_{(q_0)}((W_u v)_0) \mathfrak{g}_{(q_1)}((W_u v)_1).\]
For \(\gamma=(k,u,a)\in \Gamma\), define
\[(G_{\gamma})_{i,j} = G_{a_i(j),u(i)}.\]

nodes.label: sandwich kernel
nodes.title: sandwich kernel
nodes.statement_latex:
Let $\gamma=(k,u,a)\in \Gamma$, $X\in \mathcal{X}_k$, and $i\in [k)$. Define for  $j\in {\mathbb Z}$ and $y\in ({\mathbb R}^{2})^k$,
\begin{equation} (\mathbf{M}(\gamma,X,i))_j(y) =  \Big(\prod_{m\in [i)} (G_{\gamma})_{m,j}(y_m) \Big) X_{i,j}(y_i) \Big(\prod_{m=i+1}^{k-1} (G_{\gamma})_{m,j-1}(y_m) \Big).\end{equation}
nodes.statement_html:
Let \(\gamma=(k,u,a)\in \Gamma\), \(X\in \mathcal{X}_k\), and \(i\in [k)\). Define for \(j\in {\mathbb Z}\) and \(y\in ({\mathbb R}^{2})^k\),
\[(\mathbf{M}(\gamma,X,i))_j(y) = \Big(\prod_{m\in [i)} (G_{\gamma})_{m,j}(y_m) \Big) X_{i,j}(y_i) \Big(\prod_{m=i+1}^{k-1} (G_{\gamma})_{m,j-1}(y_m) \Big).\]

nodes.label: auto:Gaussian-difference-kernel-definition
nodes.title: difference of 2D Gaussians
nodes.statement_latex:
Let $\gamma=(k,u,a)\in \Gamma$.  For $i\in [k)$, $j\in {\mathbb Z}$, define
\begin{equation} (Y_\gamma)_{i,j} = (G_\gamma)_{i,j-1} - (G_\gamma)_{i,j}\ .\end{equation}
nodes.statement_html:
Let \(\gamma=(k,u,a)\in \Gamma\). For \(i\in [k)\), \(j\in {\mathbb Z}\), define
\[(Y_\gamma)_{i,j} = (G_\gamma)_{i,j-1} - (G_\gamma)_{i,j}\ .\]

nodes.label: telescoping terms
nodes.title: telescoping terms
used_by: vanishing diagonal implies induct positive terms
nodes.statement_html:
Let \(\gamma=(k,u,a)\in \Gamma\). Then \(Y_\gamma\in \mathcal{X}_k\) and
\[\|\sum_{i\in [k)} \mathbf{M}(\gamma,Y_\gamma,i)\|_{{\rm M}(k)}\le 2.\]

nodes.label: positive terms
nodes.title: positive terms
used_by: vanishing diagonal implies induct positive terms
nodes.statement_html:
Let \(\gamma=(k,u,a)\in \Gamma\). Let \(X\in \mathcal{X}_k\) and assume for each \(i\in [k)\) and \(j\in {\mathbb Z}\) we have \(X_{i,j}(u,v)=f_{i,j}(u)f_{i,j}(v)\) for some real valued \(f_{i,j}\in W_0({\mathbb R})\). Then for each \(i\in [k)\), \(j\in{\mathbb Z}\), and for all \(\mathbf{F}\in {\mathfrak{F}}\),
\[\Lambda_k(\mathbf{M}(\gamma,X,i)_j)(\mathbf{F})\ge 0.\]

nodes.label: square root Gaussian difference
nodes.title: square root Gaussian difference
nodes.statement_html:
Let \(a\in A\) and \(j\in{\mathbb Z}\). Define the function \(s(a,j):{\mathbb R} \to {\mathbb R}\) by
\[s(a,j) = \mathcal{F}^{-1}(\xi \mapsto \sqrt{\mathfrak{g}(a(j-1)\xi)-\mathfrak{g}(a(j) \xi)}).\]

nodes.label: s multiplier
nodes.title: s multiplier
nodes.statement_html:
Let \(\gamma=(k,u,a)\in \Gamma\). Let \(i\in [k)\) and \(j\in {\mathbb Z}\). Define \((s_{\gamma})_{i,j}: {\mathbb R} \to {\mathbb R}\) by
\[(s_{\gamma})_{i,j}=s(b,j)\]
with
\[b(j)=\sqrt{a_{i}^0(j)^2 + a_{i}^1(j)^2}\]
if \(u_i=0\), and by
\[(s_{\gamma})_{i,j}=s(\sqrt{2}a_{i}^1,j)\]
if \(u_i=1\).

nodes.label: square root Gaussian difference W0
nodes.title: Proposition: square root Gaussian difference W0
nodes.statement_latex:
For every $a\in\mathrm{A}$ and $j\in\mathbb{Z}$
we have that $s(a,j)$ is a well-defined function in $W_0({\mathbb R})$. Consequently, if $\gamma \in \Gamma$ and $i\in [k)$, $j\in {\mathbb Z}$, then $(s_{\gamma})_{i,j}$ is a well-defined function in $W_0({\mathbb R})$.
nodes.statement_html: For every \(a\in\mathrm{A}\) and \(j\in\mathbb{Z}\) we have that \(s(a,j)\) is a well-defined function in \(W_0({\mathbb R})\). Consequently, if \(\gamma \in \Gamma\) and \(i\in [k)\), \(j\in {\mathbb Z}\), then \((s_{\gamma})_{i,j}\) is a well-defined function in \(W_0({\mathbb R})\).

nodes.label: H multiplier
nodes.title: H multiplier
nodes.statement_html:
Let \(\gamma=(k,u,a)\in \Gamma\). Define \(H_{\gamma}=(H_\gamma)_{i\in [k),j\in {\mathbb Z}}\) by
\[(H_{\gamma})_{i,j}:=(s_{\gamma})_{i,j}\otimes (s_{\gamma})_{i,j} -(Y_{\gamma})_{i,j}\]
for every \(i\in [k), j\in\mathbb{Z}\).

nodes.label: H-in-X
nodes.title: Proposition: H-in-X
nodes.statement_latex: Let $\gamma=(k,u,a)\in \Gamma$. Then $H_{\gamma}\in \mathcal{X}_k$.
nodes.statement_html: Let \(\gamma=(k,u,a)\in \Gamma\). Then \(H_{\gamma}\in \mathcal{X}_k\).

nodes.label: H vanishing
nodes.title: H vanishing
nodes.statement_html:
For \(\gamma=(k,u,a)\in \Gamma\), \(i\in [k)\), \(j\in {\mathbb Z}\), and \(\xi\in {\mathbb R}\),
\[\widehat{(H_{\gamma})_{i,j}}(\xi,-\xi)=0\, .\]

nodes.label: H vanishing integral
nodes.title: H vanishing integral
nodes.statement_html:
For \(\gamma=(k,u,a)\in \Gamma\), \(i\in [k)\), \(j\in {\mathbb Z}\), and \(z\in {\mathbb R}\),
\[\int_{{\mathbb R}} (H_{\gamma})_{i,j}(z+p,p)\,dp=0.\]

nodes.label: auto:L-kernel-definition
nodes.title: Definition: auto:L-kernel-definition
nodes.statement_html:
Let \(\gamma=(k,u,a)\in \Gamma\), \(i\in [k)\), \(j\in {\mathbb Z}\). For \(t>0\), we set
\[(L_{\gamma,t})_{i,j} =(H_{\gamma})_{i,j} \ast_{(1,1)} \Phi_{(t)}.\]

nodes.label: L:F_t
nodes.title: Lemma: L:F_t
nodes.statement_html:
Let \(\gamma=(k,u,a)\in \Gamma\) and \(t>0\). Then \(L_{\gamma,t} \in \mathcal{X}_k\) and for \(i\in [k)\), \(j\in {\mathbb Z}\), we have
\[\lim_{t\to 0_+} (L_{\gamma,t})_{i,j} = (H_{\gamma})_{i,j} \quad\text{in}\;L^1.\]

nodes.label: L:ft-infty
nodes.title: Lemma: L:ft-infty
nodes.statement_html:
Let \(\gamma=(k,u,a)\in \Gamma\), \(i\in [k)\), \(j\in {\mathbb Z}\), \(t>0\). Then
\[\lim_{t\to \infty} (L_{\gamma,t})_{i,j} = 0 \quad\text{in}\;L^1.\]

nodes.label: L multiplier
nodes.title: L multiplier
nodes.statement_html:
Let \(\gamma=(k,u,a)\in \Gamma\).

Define the index set
\[\mathcal{I}_{\gamma} = \{(m,0)\,:\,m\in\mathbb{Z}, m\not=0\} \cup \{(0,l)\,:\,|l|\le \Delta_{\gamma}\} \subset \mathbb{Z}^2.\]


For every \(\iota \in\mathcal{I}_{\gamma}\), we define \(L_{\gamma,\iota}=(L_{\gamma,\iota})_{i\in [k),j\in {\mathbb Z}}\) such that for \(|l|\le \Delta_{\gamma}\),
\[(L_{\gamma,(0,l)})_{i,j}:= (H_{\gamma})_{i,j} \ast_{(1,1)} (\Phi_{(a_i^1(j+l-1))}-\Phi_{(a_i^1(j+l))})\, ,\]


if \(h>0\), then
\[(L_{\gamma,(h,0)})_{i,j}:= (H_{\gamma})_{i,j} \ast_{(1,1)} (\Phi_{(2^{h-1}a_i^1(j+\Delta_{\gamma}))}-\Phi_{(2^{h}a_i^1(j+\Delta_{\gamma}))})\, ,\]
and if \(h<0\), then
\[(L_{\gamma,(h,0)})_{i,j}:= (H_{\gamma})_{i,j} \ast_{(1,1)} (\Phi_{(2^{h}a_i^1(j-\Delta_{\gamma}-1))}-\Phi_{(2^{h+1}a_i^1(j-\Delta_{\gamma}-1))})\, .\]

nodes.label: summation-definition
nodes.title: Summation over I_γ
nodes.statement_html:
Let \(X\) be a normed \({\mathbb R}\)-vector space. Let \(\gamma=(k,u,a)\in \Gamma\) and let \(D_\iota \in X\) for \(\iota \in \mathcal{I}_{\gamma}\). We define
\[\sum_{\iota \in \mathcal{I}_{\gamma}} D_{\iota}:=\lim_{N\to \infty} \sum_{\iota \in\mathcal{I}_{\gamma}, ~|\iota| \leq N} D_{\iota},\]
where the limit is taken in \(X\).

nodes.label: sum L multiplier convergence-L1
nodes.title: Properties of L multipliers
nodes.statement_latex:
Let $\gamma=(k,u,a)\in \Gamma$ and $\iota \in\mathcal{I}_{\gamma}$. Then
$L_{\gamma,\iota}$ is a well-defined element of $\mathcal{X}_k$. In addition, if $i
\in [k)$ and $j\in {\mathbb Z}$ then
\begin{equation}
(H_{\gamma})_{i,j} = \sum_{\iota \in\mathcal{I}_{\gamma}} (L_{\gamma,\iota})_{i,j},
\end{equation}
where the sum on the right converges in $L^1$.
nodes.statement_html:
Let \(\gamma=(k,u,a)\in \Gamma\) and \(\iota \in\mathcal{I}_{\gamma}\). Then \(L_{\gamma,\iota}\) is a well-defined element of \(\mathcal{X}_k\). In addition, if \(i \in [k)\) and \(j\in {\mathbb Z}\) then
\[(H_{\gamma})_{i,j} = \sum_{\iota \in\mathcal{I}_{\gamma}} (L_{\gamma,\iota})_{i,j},\]
where the sum on the right converges in \(L^1\).

nodes.label: sandwich sums L1
nodes.title: Lemma: sandwich sums L1
nodes.statement_latex:

Let \(c > 0\), \(N\in\mathbb{N}\). A { \((c,N)\)-window} is a Schwartz function \(\phi:{\mathbb R}\to{\mathbb R}\) such that
  1. For all \(\xi\in {\mathbb R}\), \(\widehat{\phi}\) is real and
    \[0\le \widehat{\phi}(\xi)\le 1.\]
  2. For all \(\xi\in {\mathbb R}\setminus [-1,1]\) we have
    \[\widehat{\phi}(\xi)=0.\]
  3. For all \(\xi\in [-\frac12,\frac12]\) we have
    \[\widehat{\phi}(\xi)=1.\]
  4. For all \(\xi \in [-1,1]\) and all \(m\le N\),
    \[|\widehat{\phi}^{(m)}(\xi)| \leq c.\]

nodes.statement_html:
Suppose that \(\psi:{\mathbb R}\to{\mathbb R}\) is a Schwartz function with
\[{\rm supp}(\widehat\psi)\subset\mathrm{Ann}_1(1,2^2),\]
\[|\psi(u)|\le\langle u\rangle^2,\]
and
\[|\widehat\psi^{(m)}(\xi)|\le1, \qquad m\in[3), \quad \xi\in{\mathbb R}.\]
Then for every \(t\in[1,2]\), \(J\ge1\), and every increasing sequence of integers \((k_j)_{j\in[J)}\),
\[\sum_{j\in[J)}\|A_{2^{k_j}t}(\psi)\|_2^2 \le C_{\href{nct-node:lem%3Amain_aux1}{6.65}}J^{\alpha(n)},\]
where
\[C_{\href{nct-node:lem%3Amain_aux1}{6.65}} =2^4C_{\href{nct-node:P%3Ainduct-positive-terms-reduction-whitney-product}{6.63}}.\]
